title: customer-kappa-incident-timeline-draft-jordan-patel
content:
Notes (scratchpad) - customer Kappa outage window + commands tried + draft comms

Purpose: collect breadcrumbs, quick commands, error snippets, hypotheses for postmortem + draft internal/customer comms. Quick rough timeline (working).

--- TIMELINE (working) ---
2026-02-18 08:42 UTC - first alert: elevated 5xx rate from Kappa production route (route: /v1/chat/kappa) reported by dashboards (per-route error rate spike).
2026-02-18 08:44 UTC - Pager -> oncall (me). Slack thread started (#cust-kappa-incident).
2026-02-18 08:45 UTC - Synthetic probes show 504/timeouts from edge -> backend.
2026-02-18 08:47 UTC - Confirmed increased tail latency on dedicated pool dk-pool-02 (GPU nodes).
2026-02-18 08:50 UTC - Scaled up dk-pool-02 by +2 nodes (manual) to mitigate.
2026-02-18 09:05 UTC - Errors persisted. Root cause not resolved.
2026-02-18 09:18 UTC - Rolled back model pin on route from rdx-kappa-v3 -> rdx-kappa-v2 as mitigation (suspect model hotpath).
2026-02-18 09:25 UTC - Partial recovery: error rate dropped to baseline for ~10m, then resurged.
2026-02-18 09:40 UTC - Noted correlation with large-context requests (seq_len > 4096).
2026-02-18 10:05 UTC - Continued investigation: noticed KV cache eviction flood on dk-pool-02 pods.

--- COMMANDS / QUICK CHECKS RUN (copied from shell history) ---
# check pod logs (dk-pool-02, namespace redwood-cust-kappa)
kubectl -n redwood-cust-kappa get pods -l pool=dk-pool-02 -o wide
kubectl -n redwood-cust-kappa logs pod/serving-abc-0 -c serving-runtime --since=30m | sed -n '1,200p'

# tail recent stderr to capture stack traces
kubectl -n redwood-cust-kappa exec -it pod/serving-abc-0 -c serving-runtime -- bash -lc "tail -n 500 /var/log/serving-runtime/stderr.log"

# query internal metrics for kv-cache miss spike (promql)
# increase rate() window to capture spike
rate(redwood_kv_cache_miss_total{pool="dk-pool-02",route="/v1/chat/kappa"}[5m])

# invoke failing request locally (simulate long context)
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/kappa -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACT' -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"<long_context_8k_tokens>"}]}'

# check system logs for OOM / kernel kills
journalctl -u kubelet --since "2026-02-18 08:00" | grep -i kill
# check docker/containerd oom logs
crictl ps --quiet | xargs -n1 -I{} crictl inspect {} | jq '.status' | grep -i oom

# inspect gRPC errors in serving logs (look for "grpc: ")
kubectl -n redwood-cust-kappa logs pod/serving-abc-0 -c serving-runtime --since=1h | grep -E "grpc:|deadline exceeded|context canceled" | tail -n 50

--- ERROR SNIPPETS (captured) ---
[2026-02-18T09:03:12Z] ERROR serving-runtime: request failed: rpc error: code = ResourceExhausted desc = "KV cache exceeded capacity: shard 12 evicted 1024 entries in 30s"
[2026-02-18T09:07:41Z] WARN serving-runtime: grpc: received message larger than max (size = 9216001, max = 8388608)
[2026-02-18T09:08:02Z] ERROR model-loader: quantization table mismatch for model rdx-kappa-v3 (expected checksum 0x3a7b, got 0x1f2c) - falling back to fp16 path
[2026-02-18T09:09:18Z] ERROR runtime: request processing timeout after 10000ms - context deadline exceeded
[2026-02-18T09:40:27Z] INFO autoscaler: scale up event triggered (reason=high_queue_latency)

--- QUICK HYPOTHESES (brain-dump) ---
1) KV cache eviction storm: sudden influx of long-context requests caused many new KV entries -> memory pressure -> eviction thrash -> higher tail latency and ResourceExhausted errors. Evidence: cache eviction logs, miss spike.
2) Model binary/quantization mismatch: model v3 had a quantization checksum mismatch and degraded to slower fallback path (fp16) for some workers -> higher CPU/GPU memory use + slower throughput. Evidence: quantization table mismatch log entry.
3) gRPC max message size hit for very large responses (9.2MB > 8MB default) causing immediate errors for some requests. Evidence: "grpc: received message larger than max" logs.
4) Autoscaler reaction / scale lag: scaling happens but not fast enough for tail; combined with cache churn means new pods need to warm KV cache leading to short-term errors.
5) Possible regression in new serving-runtime commit (PR #214) related to cache eviction policy.

--- MITIGATIONS / ACTIONS TAKEN ---
- rolled model pin back to v2 (09:18) -> short improvement.
- increased gRPC max message size temporarily on route (patched config) to 12MB (09:50) to avoid immediate message-size failures.
- manually scaled dk-pool-02 + added a warmup helper that preloads KV prefixes for popular session ids (temp script).
- enabled stricter request size limits in gateway to prevent abusive long-context calls (rate-limited heavy contexts).

--- OBSERVATIONS AFTER MITIGATIONS ---
- message-size errors disappeared after gRPC limit bump.
- ResourceExhausted and timeouts reduced but not eliminated.
- cache miss rate returned to baseline after warmup and scale-out (approx 09:55 - 10:10 window).

--- THINGS TO VERIFY / FOLLOW UPS ---
- reproduce locally: run long-context synthetic load against v3 with current runtime commit to confirm eviction behavior (assigned to Maya).
- validate quantization deployment path: why checksum mismatch happened for some pods (Noah). Check S3 upload and model-conversion pipeline.
- revert gRPC message-size bump to controlled limit after safe fix (we should not permanently relax if it's a DoS vector).
- add prewarm + sticky cache policy for this route or persist kv cache across restart (engineering change).
- postmortem draft + RCA: include timeline + mitigation effectiveness + follow-ups.

--- DRAFT INTERNAL/CS COMM (short) ---
Subject: Incident recap - Kappa production errors (2026-02-18) - draft
Hi Product/CS team,
Quick draft for customer-facing timeline: Kappa experienced elevated errors and timeouts on 2026-02-18 starting ~08:40 UTC. Root cause appears to be a combination of unusually large context requests which triggered cache eviction storms and a degraded execution path for recently deployed model variant (rdx-kappa-v3) on a subset of pods. We applied mitigations (rolled to v2, increased capacity, temporarily adjusted gRPC limits, and warmed caches). Errors reduced and service returned to normal by ~10:30 UTC.

We are continuing to investigate and will follow up with a detailed RCA and targeted fixes (model pipeline validation, cache policy improvements, and request-size protections). cc: SRE, Product

Notes: keep internal wording non-committal until Noah confirms quantization pipeline result.
